title: The Religion of the Sikhs
textType: Introduction to Sikh belief and history
author: dorothy-field
attributionNote: Dorothy Field wrote this short introduction for the Wisdom of the East series, edited by L. Cranmer-Byng and S. A. Kapadia. She writes as a sympathetic outside observer of the early twentieth-century Punjab, not as a Sikh authority.
description: A compact introduction to Sikhism in four chapters: the lives of the ten Gurus, the religious origins of the tradition in Hindu monotheism and its contact with Islam, the doctrines of the Sikhs, and a selection of hymns from the Guru Granth Sahib and from the Dasam Granth. Field explains the Khalsa, the Guru's authority, the place of the Granth, and the daily religious practice of the community, and she quotes the hymns at length in English.
historicalContext: The Wisdom of the East series introduced Asian religions to a popular British readership before the First World War. Field's volume appeared in 1914, when the Punjab was still the centre of the Sikh world and the Singh Sabha reforms were recent; her account reflects the colonial-era presentation of Sikhism as a monotheistic reform movement.
availabilityNote: Complete. The four chapters are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time. The acknowledgement, contents and editorial note of the series are not part of the work.
